title: Resume and checkpoint across hybrid CPU+GPU path
description:
## Goal

Drain semantics for in-flight GPU batches at SIGINT or
heartbeat-checkpoint boundary; resume from checkpoint produces
byte-identical deterministic columns vs an uninterrupted reference
run. Builds on `5f12e7ff` (CPU-only heartbeat) by adding the GPU
drain protocol from design doc §4.

## Context

Task under story `9e853c62` (Hybrid CPU+GPU executor) within epic
`gf2-sim` (`f9717e7e`). Phase 0 design doc:
`dev/active/ec530af9-pipeline-design.md` §4 (heartbeat schema v2 +
drain protocol). Wave C.2 fan-out from `75c22fa8`.

## Deliverables

1. `crates/gf2-sim/src/executor/drain.rs`:
   - `Scheduler::drain_for_checkpoint()` invoking
     `hipStreamSynchronize()` on each owned stream (NOT
     `hipDeviceSynchronize()`, per design-doc §4 note: avoid
     blocking other contexts).
   - Per-stream "in-flight batches" tally so the drain knows when
     every stream is idle.
2. Integration with `gf2-sim::checkpoint::CheckpointWriter`
   (`5f12e7ff`):
   - At heartbeat boundary, scheduler calls `drain_for_checkpoint`
     before the writer serialises.
   - Per-worker `rng_word_pos` captured AFTER the drain (so the
     resume offset is correct).
3. Resume protocol:
   - On `--resume`, the scheduler reads `worker_states[]` from the
     v2 checkpoint and restores each worker's `ChaCha20Rng` to the
     recorded `rng_word_pos`.
   - First batch after resume starts at the same offset that would
     have been computed by the uninterrupted run.
4. Hybrid resume parity test in
   `crates/gf2-sim/tests/hybrid_resume.rs` (under `--features hip`):
   - SIGINT during a 10-SNR sweep with GPU stages active at frame
     N.
   - Resume produces byte-identical
     `fer / frames / errors / mean_iters` vs uninterrupted reference
     at the same seed for 3 (rate, modulation) configurations.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] SIGINT during hybrid execution drains in-flight GPU batches
  before flushing the v2 checkpoint per design-doc §4.
- [hard] Resume from that checkpoint on the same or different host
  produces byte-identical `fer / frames / errors / mean_iters`
  vs an uninterrupted reference run at the same seed for the
  3 named DVB-T2 configurations.
- [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review` gates green.

## Non-goals

- CPU-only heartbeat (owned by `5f12e7ff`).
- Failure-mode wiring (owned by `42eac5cc`).
